subject: Numeracy
title: Making 5
objectives: Children will show 5 in different ways with fingers and objects.
Children will find two groups that make 5.
content: Fingers and parts of 5, two groups that make 5, and number bond games.
teachingActivities: Use fingers, two-colour counters and five frames to show that five can be split into two parts; always say the whole and the parts; accept all finger patterns; keep language simple: "two and three make five".
learnerActivities: Show 5 in different ways and find two groups that make 5.
assessment: Observe whether each child shows 5 in two different ways and says how many more to make 5.
expectedOutcomes: Says how many more to make 5 with support.

lessons.title: Five fingers
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show five in different ways with their fingers.
successCriteria: Shows five with fingers in two ways
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can order numbers and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Hold up one hand and say "Five fingers. Can you show me three on this hand and two on that?"
teacherActivities: Show five fingers as 5 and 0, then 3 and 2.
Let children find other ways to show five.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show five fingers as 5 and 0, then 3 and 2. Children: Children copy the finger patterns.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Three and two make five." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children find other ways to show five. Children: Child shows five another way.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many fingers are down?" Children: Child says how many.

practical.title: Finger partners
practical.safety: Keep the game gentle and seated. Accept every correct finger pattern.

differentiation.support: Show and count the fingers together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show five in four different ways.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says the two parts of five
lessons.homeConnection: Show five fingers in different ways at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show five in different ways with their fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Two colour counters
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will split five counters into two groups.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can order numbers and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show five red-and-yellow counters and say "Let us see how many red and how many yellow."
teacherActivities: Shake five counters and drop them on the mat.
Say "Two red and three yellow make five."
Let each child shake and say the parts.
learnerActivities: Child shakes and says the parts.
Child puts counters in a five frame.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Shake five counters and drop them on the mat. Children: Children count red and yellow.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Two red and three yellow make five." Children: Children repeat the sentence.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child shake and say the parts. Children: Child shakes and says the parts.
Step 4. Teacher: Record the parts with counters. Children: Child puts counters in a five frame.

practical.title: Shake and spill
practical.safety: Use large two-colour counters and drop them over a tray. Keep floors clear of loose counters.

differentiation.support: Use counters of three and four with clear colours.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find all the ways to make five.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say five.
lessons.homeConnection: Split five objects into two groups.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "split five counters into two groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: How many more to make five?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find how many more are needed to make five.
successCriteria: Says how many more make five
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can order numbers and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show three counters in a five frame and say "How many more do we need to make five?"
teacherActivities: Show counters in a five frame and ask how many more.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show counters in a five frame and ask how many more. Children: Children say the number.
Step 2. Teacher: Check by adding counters. Children: Children count to five.
Step 3. Teacher: Try other starting numbers. Children: Child says how many more.
Step 4. Teacher: Play the game with partners. Children: Pairs ask each other.

practical.title: Fill the five frame
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep frames on the mat.

differentiation.support: Use counters of three or four in the frame.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to try making ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says how many more to make five
lessons.conclusion: Put the frames away and say five.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask how many more to make five at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find how many more are needed to make five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Hidden counters
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will play a hiding game that finds the hidden part of five.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can order numbers and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Show five counters and say "I will hide some. How many are hidden?"
teacherActivities: Show five counters then hide some under a cup.
Let children hide counters for a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show five counters then hide some under a cup. Children: Children count what is left.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many are hiding?" Children: Child says the number.
Step 3. Teacher: Lift the cup to check. Children: Children cheer.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children hide counters for a friend. Children: Child hides some counters.

practical.title: Hide and find
practical.safety: Use large counters and keep the game seated and gentle. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Use three counters instead of five.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to play with six or seven counters.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says the two parts of five
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say five.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a hiding game with five objects.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a hiding game that finds the hidden part of five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 making five check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child makes and splits five.
successCriteria: Says how many more to make five
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can order numbers and find one more and one less.
lessons.starter: Sing the five song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: fingers, counters and hidden counters.
At each station ask "How many more make five?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: fingers, counters and hidden counters. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many more make five?" Children: Child answers with a number.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Making five stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numbers to four.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to make six in different ways.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: shows five in different ways; splits five into two parts; says how many more to make five; finds hidden parts.

questions.question: How many more to make five from two?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing making five games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child makes and splits five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
